Charging & energy

The hybrid part an EV app doesn't have

Charging

Charging power
— kW
Off the charger or the car's charging screen

On a BYD hybrid — Sealion 6 or Shark 6 — this sits right under the range as a banner: “Remaining time 2 h 19 min · 6.4 kW” while it charges. A plug-in hybrid battery is small (18.4 kWh here), so most charging is slower AC charging at home, not just DC fast charging.

  • Scheduled charging — set a start time to use cheaper off-peak power. BYD lets you set this in the app; here it has to be set in the car until Chery Australia switches on a live connection.
  • Live charging status from the car — plugged in, charging, finished or fault, pulled straight from the car.

Energy — read both fuels together

Petrol used
— L/100 km
Last trip / average, off the car's trip screen
Electricity used
— kWh/100 km
Last trip / average, off the car's trip screen

This is the biggest hybrid difference. A fully electric app only shows kWh/100 km, and a petrol app only shows L/100 km. A hybrid uses both on the same trip — so a very low L/100 km figure on its own can mislead: it may just mean the trip ran mostly on battery. BYD's hybrid app has its own Energy Consumption screen for exactly this reason. Always read the two figures side by side, and note the drive mode: EV = electric only, engine off; HEV = petrol engine and electric motor working together, with the engine also topping up the battery.

    What works, what waits

    Working now

    • Hybrid dashboard — EV-only range (max 95 km), petrol range and total hybrid range (max 1,200 km), from readings you copy off the car's screens
    • Tyre pressures for all four wheels
    • Vehicle status line — switched off / driving / charging, EV or HEV drive mode, doors and locked state, and any dash fault — entered by hand, the way BYD's hybrid homepage shows it live
    • Charging power and time to full charge, worked out from the battery % and kW you enter
    • Energy read both ways — petrol L/100 km and electricity kWh/100 km side by side
    • Parked spot marked from this phone's GPS, with a walk-back link
    • Fuel, charge and service log in Australian dollars

    Waiting on Chery Australia

    • Remote lock and unlock (separate buttons), windows, boot, flash, horn, climate and seats
    • Live battery, fuel and location pulled straight from the car, including the car's own vehicle position
    • Live doors, windows, boot, bonnet, seats, climate cabin temperature and security status
    • Live charging, scheduled charging set from the phone, digital key, and trip and energy history from the car itself

    Chery's full app is called CarLinko. It's live in Malaysia and the UAE with dealer activation, but Chery Australia hasn't switched on a connected service here yet. When they do, the controls above are ready to wire in.

    Don't use “Chery Connect”. The app by that name on the App Store is the official Chery Israel app — it's in Hebrew and tied to the Israeli importer. It isn't the Australian app, and it can't connect to your car here.

    Checked against BYD's hybrid app

    BYD's hybrids in Australia are the Sealion 6 and Shark 6 plug-in hybrids. Their app is not the same as the fully electric BYD app — for a hybrid it shows, all on the homepage:

    • Total range with battery % and fuel % together — e.g. 548 km, 87% battery, 40% fuel. This app already did that, and still does.
    • Charging power and remaining time while plugged in — now added here, worked out from your entered kW.
    • Lock and Unlock as separate controls, plus doors / windows / seats / tyres status screens — Unlock and Seats now added; status screens now listed, with doors and locked state enterable by hand.
    • Vehicle state, faults and energy use — switched off / driving / charging, any fault, and energy in both L/100 km and kWh/100 km. Now added here.

    Sources: BYD Australia — MY BYD app (door lock/unlock, seat ventilation and heating, flashing lights and whistle, door / window / tyre pressure status, charging power, battery percentage, remaining charging time, vehicle location, predicted time to full charge) and the BYD Shark 6 owner's manual, “Vehicle Condition and Control” (homepage shows remaining range, SOC, fault information, and driving, charging, A/C, door and window, seat heater / ventilator and tyre pressure status).

    Final check — tested before release

    Every feature in this final version was checked one by one. This is the only version — use this one on your phone.

    • Dashboard update — works. Enter battery %, EV range, petrol % and petrol range and the hero updates: total = EV + petrol, capped at 95 km EV and 1,200 km total, with litres and kWh left worked out.
    • Tyres, odometer & glance tiles — works. All four kPa values show, and the lowest tyre is picked out automatically.
    • Status line & “Closed but not locked” — works. Vehicle state, EV / HEV mode, doors, locked state and dash fault update from the form, with the BYD-style warning when doors are closed but not locked.
    • Charging & energy — works. Time to full is calculated from battery % and kW entered; petrol L/100 km and electricity kWh/100 km show side by side.
    • Parked spot & trip log — works. “Mark where I parked” uses phone GPS and opens a walk-back link in Apple Maps. Petrol / Charge / Service / Trip entries add to the log in A$ for this visit.
    • Remote controls — present, correctly blocked. Lock, Unlock, Windows, Boot, Flash, Horn, Climate and Seats all tap through to a clear message: they need a live connection Chery Australia has not switched on. They do not pretend to work.
    • Phone layout — works. No sideways scrolling on iPhone width, bottom tab bar (Home / Vehicle / Log / More) scrolls to the right section, and dark mode follows your phone setting.

    Request to Chery Australia — ready to send

    For the features marked “Later”, Chery Australia / your dealer must activate a connected service for your VIN. Copy this wording, add your VIN and rego, and send it to Chery Australia — 1800 424 379 / info@cherymotor.com.au — or hand it to your dealer.

    Hello, I own a Chery Tiggo 8 Super Hybrid in Australia. VIN: __________   Rego: __________

    Please advise, for my VIN, whether CarLinko or any Chery connected service is available in Australia, and how it is activated by the dealer.

    I am requesting: remote lock and unlock, windows, boot, flash, horn, climate and seat heating / ventilation, live battery, fuel and range, live vehicle location, live doors / windows / security status, charge scheduling and time to full charge, and service / trip history from the car.

    If it is not available in Australia yet, please confirm that in writing and advise the expected timing. Thank you.

    Do not use the “Chery Connect” app from the App Store for this — that is the Israel app in Hebrew and cannot connect to an Australian car.

    Install on your iPhone — step by step

    This is the one final version. Do these steps in Safari on your iPhone 17 Pro Max — not inside another app’s browser.

    1. Open this page in Safari. If you are viewing it inside Muse, tap the link / open-in-browser option and choose Safari, so the page is open in Safari itself.
    2. Find Share. In Safari, look at the bottom of the screen (on iPhone, the toolbar at the very bottom). Tap Share — the square with an arrow pointing up . If you don’t see the toolbar, tap once near the bottom or scroll up slightly and it will appear.
    3. Scroll down in the Share sheet and tap Add to Home Screen. You may need to swipe up on the list of options to see it.
    4. Check the name. It should say Tiggo 8. Leave it as is, or edit it if you like.
    5. Tap Add at the top right of that screen.
    6. Go to your Home Screen. You will see the Tiggo 8 icon there, like a normal app.
    7. Tap the Tiggo 8 icon to open it. It opens full-screen, with no Safari bars — like the GAC and BYD apps.
    8. First use: scroll to Update readings, copy the figures off the car’s screens (battery %, EV km, petrol %, petrol km, odometer, tyre kPa), then tap Update dashboard. The top of the app will fill in.

    If “Add to Home Screen” is missing: you are not in Safari, or the page opened inside another app. Close it, open Safari, paste / open this page’s link in Safari, then repeat steps 2–5.
    To remove an older copy: press and hold the old Tiggo icon on your Home Screen → Remove App → Delete App, then keep only this final Tiggo 8 icon.
    Please note: this Home Screen version keeps readings and log entries only while it is open — closing it clears them, so enter fresh readings each trip.
